newsitem.title: UK: Oil product tanker rates to stay firm - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Oil product tanker rates to stay firm - analysts.

text.p: Freight rates for clean product tankers have soared this month and some brokers expect the rise to continue for another week or two at least.
Brokers H. Clarkson say worldwide product rates soared to $18,854 per day in the week to January 10, against a 1996 average of just $12,902.
"Rates have risen on a shortage of tonnage and demand in the U.S.," said Clarkson analyst Nicola Williams.

Almost one million tonnes of European finished and unfinished gasoline has been chartered to cross the Atlantic since the end of December, although a sharp fall in U.S. gasoline prices has now banged the arbitrage window shut.
Demand is also strong in the Mediterranean, India and the Far East.
"India is in the midst of an industrial revolution," one broker said, referring to the country's economic liberalisation programme. "I can see this (rise in product rates) lasting a bit longer."
A Med broker was also bullish. "There are lots of cargoes, especially gas oil and there are no prompt vessels. It is difficult even to the end of January."
"I think (the high rates) could last for another week, maybe two."
Clarkson said Med/UKC rates for 28,000 tonne vessels had risen to almost $17,000 per day last week from $13,100 the previous week.
They also said rates from the Middle East to Japan for 55,000 tonne ships had soared to $24,309 per day last week from an average of $18,380 in 1996.
A Norwegian broker said it was normal for rates on this route to firm sharply between October and March, and he was bullish about product rates over the next few weeks.
"Optimistic? Definitely," he said. "I think the firmness will continue on most routes."
